approach.method_basis: The Parent searches a persistent forest of molecular graph edits rooted at the supplied molecules. It scores each eligible first expansion directly, stores every actual return on its own path, and selects branches using the best completed returns of structurally similar siblings together with completed and pending visit counts. Its roots stay fixed throughout the session. A complete accepted archive supplies crossover donors, while canonical novelty checks and bounded fallbacks govern every purchase.
approach.novelty: Promote a newly observed global incumbent to the sole root of a fresh active tree after its whole feedback batch has been reconciled. This gives the next search an immediate origin at an actual discovery, with fresh path statistics and one explicitly cached context receipt. The hypothesis is that more discoveries will receive useful descendant refinements. The frozen brief has no completed same-Parent children. The concurrent root-consumer experiment changes exploitation among roots; this experiment changes the origin and lifetime of the active tree. The existing direct-frontier evaluation law is retained.

observed_bottleneck: The fixed-origin lifecycle in code Parent n-85acb9fe7124 leaves some newly observed best molecules without later path-local refinement. Its complete three-seed macro mean is 0.34810111812588734 (population deviation 0.044753851725843695), +0.021316352059607652 against its own Parent n-5cc901d1a9e3, but below formal Anchor n-cf8d309c06de at 0.607030316211131. The actual Parent summaries and run logs are successful, despite the nonfatal scheduler warning. An independent full-panel receipt audit reproduces 4,350 optimizer receipts, 62 strict chronological improvements, and 60 new post-observe incumbent opportunities with future announcements. Only 44/60 have a later accepted descendant on their original occurrence path; 16 have none. There is one zero-opportunity session, retained in the panel. Across these opportunity paths there are 439 distinct later accepted descendant receipts, 73 beating at least one associated incumbent score, and 17 making a new session incumbent; overlap is deduplicated by session receipt, and none of these associations proves mediation or supplies a missing score. Full/late gain rates are 0.00048141036925371776 and 0.0005054135173205042. The source tree ancestor demonstrates implemented peak-memory credit, not an inherited guarantee of useful restart. adoptions.applicability: The Parent exposes accepted improved molecules that can immediately serve as graph-edit origins; useful downstream refinement remains unproved.
adoptions.borrowed_element: Use a found solution as the next tree origin (Section 3.3).

deviations.adopted_setting: Strict molecular incumbent improvement triggers a fresh tree; original normalization, best-return selection and generation remain.
deviations.paper_setting: Scheduled truss-design rounds, structural objective and separately changed backup and widths.
deviations.reason: Isolate solution-to-root feedback under the frozen molecular budget; source schedules, rewards and performance do not transfer.

adoptions.implementation_change: PrefixTreeSearch.observe calls a fresh-root helper after reconciliation and strict accepted improvement, retaining the global ledger and initializing one cached context receipt.

literature_review.conclusion: Reuse the frozen review and its recorded queries; no new search query was issued. Both primary PDFs were opened directly, checking the truss update in Section 3.3 and SameGame Sections 4.1-4.2. B1 is the independently reproduced 16/60 missed descendant opportunities in the actual Parent. B3 combines the solution-to-origin element with the contrary risk of losing breadth. Only that root-reuse element is adopted; random-seed restarts, new backup laws, structural rewards and width schedules are excluded. This is an evidence-supported component hypothesis whose activation, useful conversion and endpoint result must each be measured.

sources.applicability: Borrow only observed-solution-to-new-root feedback. Adapt to a strictly improved current-session molecular incumbent at an observe boundary, fresh active-tree statistics and unchanged graph operators. Do not import structural rewards, width schedules or source performance. This is component development of the existing tree route, not IMCTS reproduction.
sources.finding: Sections 3.1–3.3 construct successive trees using a found design as the next initial design; the source separately changes backup and width schedules.
sources.title: Improved Monte Carlo tree search formulation with multiple root nodes for discrete sizing optimization of truss structures

sources.applicability: Contrary condition for incumbent-root commitment. Root relocation may discard useful breadth and is not presumed beneficial. It also contextualizes the existing peak-memory component; the measured root-mean/no-rollout combination comes from campaign evidence, not this paper.
sources.finding: Single-player search can retain all initial alternatives; exploitation of promising lines may become locally trapped, motivating restarts.
sources.title: Single-Player Monte-Carlo Tree Search

hypothesis: Change only the active-tree root lifecycle: preserve the initial forest until a complete observe boundary strictly improves the global accepted incumbent and budget remains; then discard the old active tree and instantiate a fresh single-root tree at the earliest accepted receipt attaining the new maximum. Reuse that receipt once as root context, without a new evaluation or inherited path visits. Subsequent search uses the same direct-frontier and sibling best-return controller on the new origin. This is the frozen obstacle intervention on access to discovered states, not another rollout-horizon adjustment or a root-mean consumer combination.

finding_summary.headline: Every promoted incumbent received a descendant, useful refinements rose, and mean score gained 0.1514 over the Parent
finding_summary.insights:
The missing access to newly discovered incumbents was a useful obstacle to address on this tree: the result goes beyond mechanically enlarging descendant ancestry because actual new-incumbent receipts and full and late gain rates also increased. The adopted solution-to-new-root element operated successfully in its molecular adaptation; it does not validate the source paper’s scheduling, backup or width changes. The experiment prices the complete lifecycle change, so it cannot separate improved access from erased statistics, reset depth or removed root competition. Discarding 2,779 occurrence occupancies, including 240 root occupancies, did not prevent this matched Parent gain, but the rewards of abandoned branches remain unknown.

The search still shows local proposal limitations. Full and late fragment-excluded similarity increased from 0.2985/0.3214 to 0.3888/0.4332, while panel-wide typed scaffold coverage grew; this is more concentrated local refinement, not uniform scaffold collapse. All three zaleplon sessions had no late gain. In one of them, 6,621 internal invalid actions occurred after the last improvement, including 6,618 from single-atom halogen branches; 6,463 were crossover attempts. The unchanged generator can therefore spend substantial effort on structural dead ends despite successful incumbent reuse. Molecules below six heavy atoms barely changed (432 to 425), while those above fifty rose from 165 to 301. The Molecular assessment finds useful ring, amine and carbonyl arrangements but inconsistent preservation of those relationships through edits and grafts. Proposal operators that preserve informative ring and functional-group arrangements, or search schemes that retain alternative productive origins, are plausible ways to address these observed limitations; their benefit remains untested. The evidence establishes this intervention’s useful contribution under the matched conditions while leaving the gap to the stronger Anchor and broader transfer open.
finding_summary.results: All 15 Search sessions completed. The 114 eligible improvements produced exactly 114 fresh roots, with no transferred visits or extra billed labels. Every root received a novel accepted descendant at the next announcement, compared with 44 of 60 opportunities in the Parent; the median first-descendant delay fell from two announcements to one. Unique descendants that created a new global incumbent rose from 17 to 134 out of 4,350 paid proposals. Full gain per proposal rose from 0.0004814 to 0.0010035, and late gain per proposal from 0.0005054 to 0.0006287. Thus both access and useful refinement passed their registered tests. Mean final score rose from 0.348101 to 0.499496, a gain of 0.151395, with 13 improved cells, one unchanged cell and one small loss. All three seed means improved. The formal Anchor remains higher at 0.607030, leaving a mean gap of 0.107534. The one session with no improvement kept its initial forest throughout.

molecular.headline: Rich aromatic and saturated ring chemistry reaches amino-aromatic leaders, but reactive bonds, size extremes and unspecified stereochemistry persist.
molecular.overall_character: This assessment concerns n-e4b751133c75 and published code Parent n-85acb9fe7124 on the frozen Search seeds 0, 1 and 2. All five tasks have 900 accepted records, including 870 optimizer molecules; supplied initial molecules are kept separate from generated output. context.comparison marks both Child evaluation and Parent pairing complete. All 15 trusted Child staging trajectories and 15 published Parent trajectories were read; none was missing. Child evidence is still in the exact request-listed .worktrees/slot-1/runs/staging seed directories, not a prospective node archive. Parent evidence is the actual nodes/n-85acb9fe7124/seed-0, seed-1 and seed-2 trajectory files. The run-relative audit policy/scratch/r0054-01-improve-L01-molecular/chemistry_reading.json and its per-seed/task audit files record every underlying file, its actual staging or published status, SHA256, and derived descriptors. No formal Anchor molecular comparison was performed; it is not substituted for the code Parent comparison. The digest ring-closure presence rates span 0.8402 to 0.8885 and aromatic-token presence rates 0.6828 to 0.8207; these are molecule-level text counters, not aromatic-atom fractions. RDKit reading of accepted optimizer graphs shows many fused, bridged and linked heterocycles, aryl ethers, amides, thioamides, amines, phenols, acetals and halogenated aromatics. Diversity is broad over the full panel, although leaders concentrate within related scaffold neighbourhoods. Across 4350 optimizer records per panel, the Child has 425 molecules below six heavy atoms versus Parent 432, and 301 above fifty versus Parent 165. The late 2175-record sets, optimizer ordinals 146 through 290, contain 195 versus 240 below six and 204 versus 108 above fifty. Thus loss of useful framework into fragments and enlargement into joined assemblies coexist. These are descriptive tails, not proposed admission thresholds. Several leaders look like medicinal-chemistry frameworks, but N-halogen and O-halogen bonds, peroxide or hydrazine connections, small fused rings and unspecified saturated stereochemistry limit confidence in their preparation and stability. The accepted trajectories establish graph validity, not synthetic routes; they do not measure rejected proposals or physical target binding. Score-gradient statements below are local associations in these observed molecules, not component attribution or mechanism activation.

per_task.generated_character: Generated molecules range from isolated atoms to 65-heavy-atom assemblies, with median 24 heavy atoms and three perceived rings. The strongest seed-0 and seed-1 examples each have 24 heavy atoms and four rings: halophenyl carboxamides attached to compact fused nitrogen/oxygen-containing systems. The seed-0 framework includes a small fused oxygen ring, whereas the seed-1 leader is an N-methyl indole-like carboxamide with an O-containing annulation and benzylamide substituent. The seed-2 leader instead has 25 heavy atoms, a fused/bridged imine-thioamide system, chlorophenyl group, alcohol and hydroxymethyl group. The full generated set has 404 nonempty typed Murcko scaffolds versus Parent 398; this is not total scaffold collapse. Parent seed leaders occupy related indole/thioamide, aryl-hydrazine and pyrazoline chemistry rather than these exact new annulated arrangements.
liabilities: Small annulated oxygen rings and unusual bridged thioamide/imine arrangements make synthetic feasibility uncertain even at the top of the observed score range.
Low-score tail molecules include O-halogen and peroxide-like fragments; late joined structures lose the compact functional-group relationships visible in the leaders.
missing_features: Reliable retention of the compact ring/carboxamide or ring/thioamide arrangement is missing from many purchases: 101 generated graphs fall below six heavy atoms, while 15 exceed fifty. The useful size and polarity balance is accessible but not consistently preserved.
The leading saturated fused and bridged alternatives have no specified stereochemistry. These records do not establish whether any absent stereoisomer or unseen target scaffold would score better.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The two compact annulated carboxamides both score 0.42348216717712805. A less annulated methoxy N-methyl indole carboxamide scores 0.4051924293365408, and the thioamide/alcohol leader scores 0.4031937733859023. These examples favour retaining a moderate-sized aromatic/polar framework over the zero-scoring OCl, OSCl and OOCl fragments. F-to-Cl or F-to-Br substitution in the leading families retains the same recorded maximum, so the data do not identify one privileged halogen. The final seed-2 purchase is a large joined amide/ester-like assembly scoring 3.454378382179808e-22, not the retained incumbent. Child/Parent seed endpoints are 0.42348216717712805/0.3957609793331631, 0.42348216717712805/0.4238198477630873 and 0.4031937733859023/0.37487325032997193. The middle pair prevents describing all three structural changes as improvements.

per_task.generated_character: This is the largest Child output distribution: median 32 heavy atoms and four rings, with the upper tail reaching 115 heavy atoms. The seed-1 leader is a 33-heavy-atom, four-ring, extensively heteroaromatic aryl-ether assembly with methoxy, branched fluoroalkyl and aryl-fluoride substitution plus an N-Br bond. The seed-0 leader has 43 heavy atoms and seven rings, joining repeated aza-thioamide-containing ring systems through carbon and sulfur-containing linkers; the seed-2 leader has 31 heavy atoms, aza-aromatic/fused lactone rings, aminomethoxy and amino substituents, and a nitrile. These are elaborate heterocyclic frameworks rather than a ring-poor search. The Child has 402 nonempty typed scaffolds versus Parent 343; median heavy-atom count is 32 versus 26. The Parent leaders include indole carboxamide/thioamide and flavone-like polyaryl frameworks. Synthetic plausibility ranges from recognizable ring/linker chemistry to reactive, heavily assembled structures.
liabilities: The leading aromatic nitrogen is directly brominated; related high scorers carry acyl fluoride or S-F functionality. These motifs raise stability and handling questions that the numerical score does not resolve.
Repeated heterocyclic assemblies produce a large upper size tail, especially late in search; peroxide fragments coexist at the opposite extreme.
missing_features: Controlled elaboration that retains a useful heteroaryl/ether arrangement without duplicating whole ring systems is unevenly represented: 133 generated molecules exceed fifty heavy atoms versus Parent 55, while the strongest example has 33.

The high-scoring neighbourhood does not establish a robust family of equally effective, chemically conventional replacements for its N-Br and occasional acyl-fluoride substituents. The records do not prove that stability itself is rewarded.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The heteroaryl-ether leader scores 0.6354531001589825, versus 0.5852068576121547 for the larger repeated thioamide system and 0.581008100810081 for the nitrile/lactone framework. The corresponding Parent endpoints are 0.5560224089635855, 0.5619968267027091 and 0.5615419466888167 respectively. A close heteroaryl-ether analogue with one fewer aromatic nitrogen scores 0.6342216444588885, consistent with sensitivity to fine heteroaromatic arrangement rather than size alone. Small peroxide-containing CCOOC and COO molecules still score 0.5, whereas a compact sulfur-dioxide-containing fused ring scores 0.25043702473560003. Consequently a substantial baseline score can occur without useful ring chemistry; the observed reward above that baseline associates with specific decorated multi-ring arrangements. Nothing here identifies N-bromination or increasing molecular size as a necessary source of reward.

per_task.generated_character: The Child reaches mixed aromatic/saturated amino frameworks across all seeds. Its generated median is 30 heavy atoms and three rings, versus Parent 25 heavy atoms and three rings. The seed-1 leader has 28 heavy atoms and four rings: an N-butyl tertiary ring amine within an O-containing fused framework, a diarylamine link, methoxy group and halogenated aryl ring. The seed-0 leader has 34 heavy atoms and five rings, combining an N-ethyl hydroxypiperidine-like ring, a fluorinated biaryl system and an N-hydroxy saturated nitrogen ring. The seed-2 leader has 29 heavy atoms and three rings, including a phenolic/aniline-substituted fused ether framework and an aminoalkyl substituent. Nonempty typed scaffold counts are 284 versus Parent 335, so useful amino-aromatic arrangements coexist with a narrower typed-scaffold set. These are recognizable medicinal-chemistry motifs, but unusual aminal-like connections and several undefined saturated centres keep synthetic plausibility qualified.
liabilities: The best seed-0 molecule has an N-OH bond, while the seed-1 framework includes an N-C-O linkage and fused saturated ring junctions. Stability and stereochemical accessibility are not established by graph validity.

The whole set still includes 102 molecules below six heavy atoms and 54 above fifty, alongside heavily halogenated aromatic structures. Size and amino-group presence alone are insufficient descriptions of the high-score chemistry.
missing_features: Basic amino centres on or near ring systems are demonstrably accessible, so their absence is not the correct diagnosis. The missing consistency is retaining the combined amino/aromatic geometry instead of generating protected nitrogens or isolated amine fragments.

Alternative geometries and stereochemical states around the saturated fused and substituted rings remain unspecified. Fewer typed scaffolds than the Parent does not show that unvisited arrangements would be better.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The N-butyl fused amino/diarylamine leader scores 0.9687642535682931; the more saturated polycyclic amine scores 0.9190747819767275; the aminoalkyl aromatic example scores 0.8602533326723711. Their seed-matched Parent endpoints are 0.6829939673069022, 0.09970328429029204 and 0.16662005665018462 respectively. Low-scoring examples include an aza-aromatic ketone/ether with no aliphatic amine at 0.0002220008414784072 and a pyrrolidine whose ring nitrogen is sulfonylated at 0.0002562175393167918. The visible gradient therefore associates higher scores with non-amide amino centres combined with substantial aromatic framework and appropriate linkage, not simply with any nitrogen atom. The final small amino fragment scores only 0.01444130626468356. Equal maxima for aryl F/Br and O/S linker variants demonstrate tolerance within one neighbourhood; they do not establish an indispensable substituent or physical binding mechanism.

per_task.generated_character: The generated median is 30 heavy atoms and four rings, with a 107-heavy-atom upper extreme. Leaders are phenyl-substituted nitrogen heterocycles joined to substituted aromatic rings and cyclic carbonyl/ester functionality. The seed-2 maximum has 34 heavy atoms and five rings: an aryl O-Cl group, fused lactone, pyrazole-like ring and enlarged N-methyl amino/lactam-containing ring. A close methoxy-containing, O-halogen-free alternative retains the lactone and enlarged nitrogen ring. The seed-1 maximum uses a fused nitrogenous dicarbonyl system, aryl methylthio substituent and O-F bond. Seed 0 never exceeds the supplied phenolic ester/phenyl fused-dione initial molecule; that endpoint is not a generated discovery. The Child explores 431 nonempty typed scaffolds versus Parent 359, extending related dione chemistry into larger rings and lactones. Conventional carbonyl frameworks coexist with conspicuous reactive substituents.
liabilities: Aryl O-Cl and O-F bonds occur in leading examples; they are different chemistry from ordinary carbon-halogen aromatic substitution and should not be treated as routine medicinal functional groups.

Large and irregular fused/expanded ring systems have no specified stereochemistry or demonstrated synthetic route. The 74 molecules above fifty heavy atoms do not establish useful additional complexity.
missing_features: The generator does not reliably turn the accessible carbonyl-rich multi-ring arrangement into higher-scoring alternatives across all seeds: the unchanged initial seed-0 incumbent is a concrete absence of generated improvement.

Chemically conventional oxygen substitution is already possible near the top of the observed range, yet it is not consistently retained during ring enlargement and rearrangement. Nothing in these observations identifies a required unseen reference scaffold.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The O-Cl lactone/expanded nitrogen-ring leader scores 0.19720265943665388. The methoxy alternative scores 0.19388096511675595 and a methyl alternative scores 0.19350785764661843, showing that strong local scores do not require an O-halogen bond. Seed 1 reaches 0.18484422002677828 versus Parent 0.17149858514250882, while seed 2 reaches 0.19720265943665388 versus Parent 0.17425776739131107. Both seed-0 endpoints remain at the initial 0.1678386594791329. Zero-scoring S, O, C=N and N#CCCN lack the multi-ring/carbonyl arrangement. The observed gradient favours retention and rearrangement of that framework over atom-level fragments, but only modestly separates these related larger structures. The final seed-2 ester/dione derivative scores 0.15300484146274643 and is not the session maximum.

per_task.generated_character: The Child spans tiny fragments to 71-heavy-atom assemblies, with median 22 heavy atoms and two rings. The leading seed-0 family has a pyridyl-substituted pyrazoline, hydrazine-substituted thiocarbonyl and a hydroxylated unsaturated ring; its maximum adds an N-F bond and has 25 heavy atoms and three rings. The seed-1 maximum is a 22-heavy-atom phenolic/methoxy arene attached through NH to a small four-membered N-N ring, carrying N-F, C-F and O-N linkages. The seed-2 maximum has 24 heavy atoms and three rings: an amino acetal-like heterocycle with hydroxymethyl group joined to a halogenated aza-bicyclic framework. Parent leaders instead include adjacent thiocarbonyls, an N-hydroxy pyrazoline, and a fused methoxy/carboxamide nitrogen heterocycle. Typed scaffold count is 301 versus Parent 320, while generic scaffold count is 208 versus 201; neither metric alone shows uniform contraction or expansion of chemical space.
liabilities: N-F bonds occur in two seed leaders, alongside N-N or O-N connections; the small unsaturated N-N ring and crowded amino-acetal centre make synthesis and stability questionable.
The heavily substituted acetal and fused saturated frameworks carry no explicit stereochemistry. Large joined structures can combine multiple sensitive motifs without useful score.
missing_features: The search reaches compact heteroatom-rich arrangements but does not reliably preserve them: elaborate grafting can eliminate nearly all observed reward despite retaining recognizable substructures.

Stable conventional alternatives spanning the same useful donor/acceptor geometry are insufficiently established around N-F, hydrazine-thiocarbonyl, O-N and amino-acetal leaders. The data show chemical liabilities without showing that an instability penalty would improve the objective.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The compact pyridyl/thiocarbonyl series progresses from 0.37036805117359356 for a phenolic member to 0.3712227660418506 for an expanded fluoro-unsaturated ring and 0.4230032077811577 for the N-fluoro analogue. This is an observed association with changes in ring composition and heteroatom placement, not proof that N-F chemistry is desirable or causal. The small N-N-ring and amino-acetal leaders score 0.35855114551835887 and 0.36108629330282105; Parent seed endpoints are 0.22214762395800358 and 0.3203237480399838, with Parent seed 0 at 0.3421178198486577. Large grafted polycycles score zero or extremely small values, and the digest median is only 4.2e-05. Within the amino-acetal series, replacing the hydroxymethyl-bearing site with chlorine accompanies a drop to 0.0003236954852192424; the last seed-2 purchase is 0.13620030156751115. Moderate size and a particular polar/heteroatom arrangement visibly matter more than indiscriminate ring accumulation or halogenation.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-e4b751133c75, complete frozen Search seeds 0, 1 and 2, compared descriptively with published code Parent n-85acb9fe7124 under the same evaluation profile. Among 4350 optimizer records the Child retains 425 below-six-heavy-atom fragments versus Parent 432, while above-fifty-heavy-atom assemblies rise to 301 versus 165. The late subsets retain both tails, with 195 small and 204 large Child molecules. Its strongest local examples often preserve compact rings with positioned amines, carbonyls or polar substituents; both framework destruction and whole-scaffold grafting remain visible. These are properties of the accepted output distributions, not evidence about which algorithm component caused them.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably change molecular size while retaining an informative ring and functional-group framework.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator needs access to contraction, expansion and rearrangement edits that preserve potentially useful local donor/acceptor and ring relationships. Use only current-session accepted feedback to discover which sizes and arrangements matter. The observation does not establish a universal molecular-size target, a fixed admission floor/cap, or a score benefit from eliminating either tail.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-e4b751133c75 on the same complete Search panel, with n-85acb9fe7124 as the published comparison. Observed leaders contain N-Br, N-F, O-Cl, O-F, N-OH, hydrazine-thiocarbonyl and crowded amino-acetal motifs. Conventional amide, ether and amino frameworks are also reachable; one carbonyl-rich series includes an O-halogen-free methoxy member near its local maximum. Thus stable-looking chemistry is not absent, and reactivity is not proven to be required by the scores. The limitation is incomplete access to comparable conventional linkage arrangements, not a demonstrated benefit for a chemistry filter.
transferable_gaps.gap: High-scoring neighbourhoods do not consistently supply chemically conventional alternatives to reactive heteroatom linkages.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Expose chemically conservative heteroatom, bond and linker alternatives around promising graphs while preserving their useful topology, so ordinary linkages can compete through the same session feedback. Do not hard-code an objective-specific motif, infer physical activity from a score, or treat removing reactive motifs as an already validated improvement.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-e4b751133c75, frozen Search panel and code Parent n-85acb9fe7124. The Child reaches ring-associated tertiary amines, aminoalkyl aromatics, carboxamide-bearing fused rings and compact nitrogen/oxygen-rich frameworks. Low-score examples in the same observed populations instead expose isolated amines, protect nitrogen through carbonyl/sulfonyl groups, or join large frameworks without maintaining the favourable arrangement. Full-set typed scaffold counts change in both directions relative to Parent, while leaders remain concentrated within related local structural families. The evidence concerns chemical arrangement and coverage, not a blanket shortage of nitrogen, rings or diversity.
transferable_gaps.gap: Useful combinations of aromatic surfaces and polar or potentially ionizable centres are reachable but inconsistently preserved across scaffold changes.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide task-agnostic transformations that vary ring topology, linker geometry and saturation while retaining functional-group relationships when chemically meaningful. Let current-session observations determine which arrangements deserve further generation; neither importing a named scaffold nor enforcing universal amine enrichment follows from this comparison. Chemistry-score association does not isolate the contribution of any operator or controller.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-e4b751133c75 frozen digest and all accepted Search trajectories, with n-85acb9fe7124 as the matched published reference. Every task has zero stereocentre-token rate, and all 4350 Child optimizer SMILES lack explicit tetrahedral stereochemical tokens. The actual molecules nevertheless include substituted piperidine-like rings, amino acetals, fused saturated junctions and bridged alcohol-containing frameworks. The Parent shows the same unresolved representation property. Token absence does not prove achirality, nor do these records measure a reward for choosing a stereoisomer.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output does not distinguish stereochemical alternatives created by substituted saturated and bridged ring chemistry.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Where supported by the existing identity and evaluation contract, a task-agnostic representation would need to preserve and distinguish chemically meaningful stereochemical states introduced by graph edits. Treat any effect on observed scores as unmeasured; the evidence supplies no preferred stereoisomer, protonation rule or target-specific configuration.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
